explore.title: Explore by ecosystem
explore.lead: Resolve a registry name to its GitHub repository's public facts (liveness, vulnerabilities, maintainers, real-world usage).

home.orgsDesc: From repositories maintained by organizations like Google, AWS and Microsoft.
home.popularNote: Not a ranking or recommendation — representative libraries as starting points for research. Click to search.

states.errorHint: This may be temporary. Try reloading the page or come back in a moment.
states.offline: You're offline. Check your network connection (this clears automatically when you're back).

registry.resultsNote: {source} registry results ({count} · {size}/page). Resolved repositories show GitHub trust facts directly (otherwise the registry card).
registry.filteredEmpty: No packages match the filters. Try loosening them.
registry.rateLimited: Some are shown in simplified form due to GitHub rate limits (registry cards). Set GITHUB_TOKEN to resolve (anonymous 60req/h → authenticated 5,000req/h).

compare.title: Library comparison
compare.subtitle: Trust-relevant public facts, side by side. No scoring — just facts and sources (you decide).
compare.needTwo: Select 2 or more to compare. Add from “＋ Add to compare” on each card / detail page (up to 3).

check.title: Check your dependencies
check.lead: Paste package.json / composer.json and we turn it into links to each dependency's trust facts. Parsing happens in your browser — nothing is sent.
check.formats: Supported: package.json (npm) / composer.json (Composer). More ecosystems coming.
check.privacy: ※ Parsed in your browser, not uploaded

errors.appErrorBody: An unexpected error occurred while rendering this page. It may be a temporary problem.
errors.detailErrorBody: A problem occurred while fetching external data. Please try again in a moment.
errors.notFoundBody: The page you are looking for doesn't exist or may have moved. Please check the URL.
errors.globalBody: An unexpected error occurred. Please reload.

detail.metaDescription: Public, trust-relevant facts for {name} (status, vulnerabilities, maintainers, real-world usage) — with sources.
detail.licenseDeclared: Declared in {file} (GitHub couldn't map to SPDX).
detail.licenseFromText: Detected from {file} text (GitHub couldn't map to SPDX).
detail.licenseNoneNote: ※ "None detected" means GitHub couldn't find a LICENSE — it doesn't mean there is no license.
detail.licenseCustomNote: ※ A LICENSE exists but doesn't map to a known SPDX id (possibly custom/modified).
detail.checklistNote: ※ Decision material — not a pass/fail or score (you decide). Jump to details from each item.
detail.disclaimer: These are public facts and do not guarantee code correctness or the absence of undisclosed vulnerabilities. Geniesta does not score or judge — it presents facts with sources. You make the final call.
detail.fetchedAt: Fetched at {time} (see methodology for per-source refresh cadence)
detail.readEvidence: Every fact links back to its primary source. Geniesta does not score or judge — it only presents facts with sources.
detail.readTrend: Read the direction (rising/declining) first. Absolute DL counts differ by orders of magnitude across ecosystems, so comparisons are a guide. The line is a moving average (spikes smoothed).
detail.readLicense: The license shapes adoption terms. Copyleft (GPL-family) licenses can require releasing the source of derivatives on distribution; commercial/redistribution terms vary by license. We don't judge good or bad — check the license text before you adopt.
detail.renamedNote: This repository was renamed: {from} → {to} (the old URL still works)
detail.fbThanks: Thanks for the feedback (we use it to improve what we show).
detail.fbReport: Report this fact (tell us what disagrees with the source)
detail.vulnVersionNoneRest: (across the whole package there are {all} published; other versions are affected).
detail.upgradeMajor: fix in {v} (major bump — possible breaking changes)
detail.vulnDisclaimer: ※ Only published/registered advisories. Undisclosed/unregistered vulnerabilities are out of scope; this is not a safety guarantee. These advisories are for this package itself and do not cover vulnerabilities in its (transitive) dependencies.
detail.osvMatch: Cross-checked with OSV: {osv} GHSA entries agree (redundancy vs single-source).
detail.osvDiff: Cross-checked with OSV: {only} of {osv} GHSA entries are OSV-only (the GHSA query may have missed them — verify on OSV).
detail.fixSpeedNote: {n} advisories with no fix yet have been open a median of {days} days (a proxy for how slow the response is).
detail.concSolo: Tends to rely on a single maintainer (low bus factor)
detail.concFew: Tends to concentrate in a few (~3) maintainers
detail.respMedian: Median time to first response: {value} ({responded} of the last {sample} issues got a reply)
detail.respNone: No reply comments seen on the last {sample} issues (not necessarily neglect).
detail.maintainerNote: ※ Shares are a guide within the top {n} (not the full commit history). Concentration isn't bad in itself — use it as a continuity hint.
detail.healthDesc: GitHub's measure of community standard files (a guide).
detail.postureNote: ※ "Absent" doesn't mean dangerous. It's a reference fact (e.g. is there a channel for disclosure).
detail.releaseGapNote: {n} days since the latest release (median release interval is {median} days).
detail.releaseGapNoData: At least 2 published releases are needed to compute the release interval.
